clue.text: Most Africans consider themselves above those who live here!

definitions.text: Most Africans consider themselves above those who live here!

parts.words: Most Africans consider themselves above those who live here!
parts.note: reads like snobbery, but it is geography: a city at the very southern tip of the continent has nearly every other African to its north, on the map above it

explanation.surface: A sneer about continental snobbery towards the people of one place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Above' sounds like social superiority; it is literal map position, north of a city on the southern tip of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African city sits near the Cape of Good Hope, so almost all of Africa lies north of it.

clue.text: Parts of trunks containing some organs

definitions.text: Parts of trunks containing some organs

parts.words: Parts of trunks containing some organs
parts.note: trunks here are human torsos, and the upper part of each holds the heart and lungs; the luggage sense of trunks is a second meaning of the same word

explanation.surface: An anatomy description, or perhaps luggage packed with musical instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper front of the torso, housing heart and lungs, is a part of the body's trunk.

clue.text: And steals out to sea in it

definitions.text: And steals out to sea in it

parts.words: And steals out to sea in it
parts.note: the vessel in which a robber of the high seas sails out to plunder, with 'steals out' read both as slipping away and as thieving offshore

explanation.surface: Someone slips quietly out to sea in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer's vessel is the craft a sea robber steals in.

clue.text: Purloin something? Simple — relax

parts.note: to purloin is to take
it is an unspecified something
simple means easy

explanation.surface: A thief is advised that stealing is easy and to stay calm.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom telling someone to calm down and stop striving.

clue.text: Gas light!

definitions.meaning: a noble gas, element number ten
a glowing sign tube filled with that gas, as in shop-front lighting

explanation.definitionFit: The inert element is a gas, and tubes of it make the bright red signs called by its name.

clue.text: Dips, intending to clean up

definitions.meaning: washes in a tub, getting into water to get clean

explanation.definitionFit: Both a swim in the sea and a soak in the tub go by this verb.

clue.text: Well groomed girls"? Hope so!…

parts.note: groomed is taken as having a groom: women at a wedding, each with a bridegroom, are the girls who are groomed

explanation.surface: A doubtful remark about how smartly some young women are turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Women being married each have a groom, so they are literally groomed.

clue.text: and a sweet dish. Play fast and loose with her affections

definitions.meaning: a layered pudding of sponge, custard and cream

definitions.text: Play fast and loose with her affections
definitions.meaning: to toy with someone's feelings, to treat them lightly

explanation.walkthrough: A TRIFLE is a British layered dessert of sponge, fruit, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The pudding and the verb meaning to toy with someone's feelings share one spelling.

clue.text: Liver's upset-its whitish in colour, and hard

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of liver plus the S, read as 'liver is'

explanation.surface: A diseased liver turns pale and hardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges LIVERS; the 's is read as 'is', so its S counts as a letter. 'upset-its' is OCR run-together of 'upset — it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The precious metal is greyish-white and, as metals go, fairly firm.

clue.text: Novel that isn't copyright? Yes, indeed!

definitions.text: Novel that isn't copyright? Yes, indeed!

parts.words: Novel that isn't copyright? Yes, indeed!
parts.note: a novel work is fresh, and something that is not a copy is new; the publishing words copyright and novel lead the eye to books

explanation.surface: A question about whether a book is out of copyright.
explanation.definitionFit: Something new and not imitated is first of its kind.

clue.text: They're well suited to be high-fliers

definitions.text: They're well suited to be high-fliers

parts.words: They're well suited to be high-fliers
parts.note: suited means wearing protective suits, and high-fliers are those who travel far above the earth in rockets

explanation.surface: Ambitious young executives dressed smartly for success.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts wear pressure suits and fly beyond the atmosphere.

clue.text: They hear about a Pole, and how he gets his wages

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hearing organs go round the pole

parts.note: ears are what hear
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Listeners discuss a Polish worker and how he is paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish man; it is a magnetic pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Receiving pay for work is the verb for gaining money by labour.

clue.text: Take it out in a thunderstorm, perhaps

definitions.text: Take it out in a thunderstorm, perhaps

parts.words: Take it out in a thunderstorm, perhaps
parts.note: to take cover is what you do when caught out in a storm, so you 'take' this noun

explanation.surface: Advice on carrying something out into bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking cover from rain or danger is called this.

clue.text: Gets stuck into the meat roll sharpish!

definitions.text: Gets stuck into the meat roll sharpish!

parts.words: Gets stuck into the meat roll sharpish!
parts.note: reads like someone eating greedily, but describes a pointed rod pushed through a rolled joint

explanation.surface: A hungry diner tucks into a meat roll quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed metal or wooden pin is pushed through meat to hold it while cooking.

clue.text: Errant knights? His were quite the reverse!

definitions.text: Errant knights? His were quite the reverse!

parts.words: Errant knights? His were quite the reverse!
parts.note: errant knights are wanderers, but also erring; the legendary king's Round Table men were famed as models of virtue, the reverse of erring

explanation.surface: A remark on wandering knights and one master whose men were different.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary British king led the Knights of the Round Table.

clue.text: Labour with the object of becoming boss? Dissatisfied trade unionist may

definitions.text: Labour with the object of becoming boss?
definitions.meaning: read literally, to toil in order to govern
a protest in which staff follow regulations so strictly that work slows

explanation.definitionFit: An industrial protest tactic of obeying regulations to the letter, read literally as striving for power.

clue.text: Makes better parts of the feet, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: heels are the backs of the feet

explanation.surface: A remedy that cures the soles and backs of one's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure is to restore to health.

clue.text: Wren, I learn, is back inside the ship

indicators.note: is back says the hidden letters are read backwards
inside says the letters sit within the words Wren, I learn

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Wren reports that she has returned on board.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'inside the ship' as the definition, leaving the hidden word with no signal: 'inside' is that signal, and 'the ship' defines. Wrens are members of the Women's Royal Naval Service.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger ship.

clue.text: Great part of Poplar, Gerrards Cross & Wimbledon

indicators.note: part of says the letters are a portion of the place names that follow

explanation.surface: A list of London districts and home-county towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar and Wimbledon are London districts; Gerrards Cross is a Buckinghamshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Big and great are synonyms of size.

clue.text: Being in debt finishes off one, could it be said?

definitions.text: Being in debt finishes off one, could it be said?

parts.words: Being in debt finishes off one, could it be said?
parts.note: reads as debt ruining a person, but the sense is someone clearing a debt, paying it off and so finishing it

explanation.surface: A gloomy thought that debt can be the ruin of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying back money owed settles the debt.

clue.text: Sharp answer used by the chemist?

definitions.meaning: a glass vessel with a long bent neck, used for distilling in a laboratory

explanation.definitionFit: A witty riposte and a long-necked distilling flask share this name.

clue.text: Very much loved, dead or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so these letters take a different order

explanation.surface: Someone cherished, whether living or dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipped and cherished mean intensely loved.

clue.text: More than just nurse a relative!

definitions.text: More than just nurse a relative!

parts.words: More than just nurse a relative!
parts.note: a senior hospital nurse ranks above an ordinary one, and the same title names a female sibling

explanation.surface: An urge to do more than simply look after a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a ward SISTER is a senior nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a senior nurse and a female sibling.

clue.text: In the oven, a piece of meat is stored; a chop

indicators.note: to chop is to cut up, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A cook stores a piece of meat in the oven, perhaps a chop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chop' looks like a cut of meat; it rearranges STORED A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooked by dry heat in an oven describes a joint baked there.

clue.text: It's pointless, sending out plan

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
pointless means without a compass point, so the N is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone decides it is futile to post a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' drops N (north, a point of the compass) from SENDING, leaving SEDING; 'out' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a scheme or outline drawn up beforehand.

clue.text: Ersatz food eaten by them!

parts.note: reads as fake food, but ersatz describes the eaters: food is chewed by artificial teeth

explanation.surface: A complaint about substitute food in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: False teeth are artificial sets that chew food.

clue.text: Commonly, fingerprints fish

definitions.meaning: slang for fingerprints, as police say

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for fingerprints and the name of a small flatfish.

clue.text: It's ridiculous to peer at this light entertainment

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd, so the letters are made nonsense of and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds it absurd to stare at a light show.
explanation.definitionFit: A light opera is a short, comic stage entertainment.

clue.text: Delicate part of steam train?

definitions.meaning: the wagon behind a steam locomotive carrying coal and water

explanation.definitionFit: Soft or sensitive, and the coal wagon coupled behind a steam engine.

clue.text: He cuts open the head — inside, finds a fish

indicators.note: inside says the head letter goes within the surgeon

parts.note: a surgeon is a man who cuts patients open

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A surgeon opens a skull and discovers a fish within.
explanation.definitionFit: The large fish yields caviar.
